content: 1. Protease inhibitors, such as darunavir, have been associated with the development of insulin resistance. This may lead to hyperglycemia in some patients. Monitor blood glucose levels and adjust therapy as needed. 2. Cobicistat increases the plasma concentration and effect of mirtazapine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in mirtazapine metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 3. Mipomersen and darunavir may increase each other's toxicity through mechanisms that include hepatic enzyme elevation. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely when these drugs are coadministered. 4. Darunavir increases mirtazapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of adverse reactions due to elevated exposure to the cytotoxic component DM4. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Mitotane decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4. Monitor darunavir levels and adjust the dose if necessary. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This increases the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects, including Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Darunavir increases the levels of mometasone (inhaled or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 9. Nafcillin decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor darunavir levels to ensure therapeutic efficacy. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Monitor for potential adverse effects of naldemedine when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 11. Darunavir increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 12. Darunavir decreases the effects of nateglinide, potentially due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor blood glucose levels and adjust antidiabetic therapy as needed. 13. Nefazodone increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat increases nefazodone levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 14. Darunavir and nelfinavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when coadministered. Monitor for signs of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS). 15. Cobicistat increases the levels of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is required, but monitor closely for adverse effects. 16. Darunavir increases the levels of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is required, but use caution and monitor closely. 17. Darunavir and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Darunavir also increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 18. Darunavir increases the levels of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, nifedipine increases darunavir levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Darunavir increases the levels of nilotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustment of nilotinib may be necessary. Refer to nilotinib prescribing information for specific dosing instructions. 21. Darunavir increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. If adverse effects occur, consider dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein activity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed if adverse effects occur. 23. Nirmatrelvir increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased adverse effects of protease inhibitors when coadministered. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir increases the levels of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may also increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel. Monitor for adverse effects. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels of nortriptyline by an unspecified mechanism. Carefully titrate the dose of nortriptyline to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible dose, and monitor closely. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the frequency of oliceridine dosing and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 28. Darunavir increases the levels of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Adjust oliceridine dosing as needed and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 30. Darunavir increases the levels of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease ondansetron clearance, but no dosage adjustment is recommended. 31. Orlistat decreases darunavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if virological control is lost. 32. Darunavir increases the levels of osilodrostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. Darunavir increases the levels of ospemifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 34. Oxcarbazepine decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor darunavir levels to ensure therapeutic efficacy. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust oxycodone dosing as needed and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 36. Darunavir increases the levels of oxycodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the oxycodone dose if necessary and monitor closely. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels of paclitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 38. Darunavir increases the levels of panobinostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels of paricalcitol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 40. Darunavir increases the levels of paroxetine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of paroxetine based on clinical assessment of antidepressant response. 41. Pentobarbital decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor darunavir levels to ensure therapeutic efficacy. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels of perphenazine by an unspecified mechanism. A dose reduction of perphenazine may be needed when coadministered. 43. Darunavir increases the levels of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Darunavir increases the levels of pitavastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Start with the lowest recommended dose of pitavastatin and monitor for safety. 45. Darunavir increases the levels of pitolisant by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels of polatuzumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential adverse effects related to increased exposure to MMAE, a CYP3A4 substrate.
